### Symbols for units and constants

| Symbol | Meaning |
|---|---|
| $\hbar$ | reduced Planck constant |
| $c$ | speed of light |
| $k_B$ | Boltzmann constant |
| $e$ | elementary charge, $e > 0$; the electron has $q = -e$ |
| $M_{\mathrm{Pl}}$ | reduced Planck mass, $M_{\mathrm{Pl}} = (8\pi G_N)^{-1/2} = \kappa^{-1}$ |
| $T$ | temperature |
| $\beta$ | inverse temperature, $\beta = 1/(k_BT)$ |

Conventions:

- Electromagnetism is in Heaviside-Lorentz units with $c = 1$: Maxwell's equations carry no $4\pi$, and a point charge
  has the potential $\Phi = q/(4\pi r)$. SI units appear only where numbers are given; Gaussian units appear only
  in comparisons that name them.
- $\hbar$, $c$ and $k_B$ are set to $1$ only where a page says so; each tutorial lists where it does.
